answer: Submissions that land within 241 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The whisper detector writes to knoll, and sonnet publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 30 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
